description: Representative Joe Morelle (D-NY) voices his frustrations with Tennessee adopting a new map that eliminates the state’s only Democratic congressional seat. He discusses being tasked with redistricting New York state in lieu of recent events and explains how these two processes have stark differences. Rep. Morelle also talks about his support to end lawmakers from participating in prediction markets and his reaction to NY Governor Kathy Hochul announcing a $268B state budget. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: People Are Angry: Morelle on Tennessee Redistricting

author: Zoe Tillman
description: A US judge blasted the Trump administration’s Department of Government Efficiency project for relying on artificial intelligence tools as it orchestrated roughly $100 million in cuts to federal funding for humanities programs last year.
title: DOGE Slammed by Judge for Using AI to Find $100 Million in Cuts

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Courtney McBride
description: American forces responded to Iranian attacks on Navy destroyers as they were sailing in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, US Central Command said.
title: US Says It Fired on Iranian Targets After Attack on Warships

author: Erik Larson, Zoe Tillman
description: President Donald Trump’s 10% global tariffs were declared unlawful by a federal trade court in a fresh blow to the administration’s economic agenda, several months after the US Supreme Court vacated earlier levies he’d imposed.
title: Trump’s Latest 10% Tariffs Found Unlawful by US Trade Court

author: Lucy White
description: UK Energy Secretary Ed Miliband privately urged Prime Minister Keir Starmer to consider setting out a timeline for his resignation, amid concerns that losses in the local election will see him forced out of office, The Times newspaper reported.
title: UK Minister Urged Starmer to Plan Departure Timeline, Times Reports

author: Rebecca Choong Wilkins
description: When Donald Trump’s plane touches down in Beijing, he’ll become the first sitting US president to visit China in nearly a decade. His two-day summit with Xi Jinping extends a personal relationship that’s weathered a tariff war, pandemic and historic energy crisis.
title: World’s Most Important Bromance Revived as Trump Heads to China

author: Joe Mayes, Ellen Milligan
description: Keir Starmer is awaiting the results of one of the most consequential rounds of local elections in recent British history, a vote that could determine his future as prime minister and shape national policy in Europe’s second-largest economy.
title: Starmer Awaits Fate After Polls Close in Crucial UK Elections

description: On today's episode, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speaks Mike McKee, Bloomberg TV and Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent on his interview with Mary Daly. They also spoke to Jeff Simmons, President and CEO at Elanco Animal Health, Rebecca Homkes, Lecturer at the London Business School and Dr. Pattie Maes, Head of Fluid Interfaces Group at MIT Media Lab. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Awaits Iran Response on Deal, Stocks Decline From Highs | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/07/2026

author: Nancy Cook
description: There are many points of contention, but substantive deals are unlikely
title: For Trump and Xi, Low Expectations for Beijing Summit Next Week

author: David Alire Garcia
description: Trump busca el “dominio estadounidense” en la región con el mayor despliegue de tropas de EE.UU. de la historia.
title: El agresivo despliegue militar de Trump en Panamá mantiene a América Latina en vilo

description: Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz deliver insight and analysis on the latest headlines from the White House and Capitol Hill, including conversations with influential lawmakers and key figures in politics and policy. The US is waiting on Iran to respond to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end a war that’s killed thousands of people, with tensions still high in both the Persian Gulf and in Lebanon. Iran’s leaders are yet to indicate whether they’ll accept the terms of the deal, though they’ve previously shown little sign of yielding on their nuclear program and accepting a moratorium on enriching uranium, both top US demands. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Awaits Iran's Peace Deal Response | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/07/2026

description: Bill Campbell, Doubleline Global, Sovereign and Emerging Markets Head, talks about how the war with Iran is impacting markets, a lasting inflation shock and making sure markets don't lose confidence in the Federal Reserve. He speaks on a special "Bloomberg The Close" from Los Angeles. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Can't Lose Credibility, Says Doubleline's Campbell

description:
The US is waiting on Iran to respond to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end a war that’s killed thousands of people, with tensions still high in both the Persian Gulf and in Lebanon. Iran’s leaders are yet to indicate whether they’ll accept the terms of the deal, though they’ve previously shown little sign of yielding on their nuclear program and accepting a moratorium on enriching uranium, both top US demands.

Evelyn Farkas is Executive Director of the McCain Institute and Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Russia, Ukraine, and Eurasia. She speaks with Bloomberg's Kailey Leinz on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Farkas: Iran's Nuclear Program is "Number One Problem"

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump said he would give the European Union until July 4 to ratify its trade agreement with the US, after previously threatening to hike tariffs on auto imports as soon as this week if it failed to do so.
title: Trump Gives EU Until July 4 to Ink Deal, Extending Deadline

description:
The Trump administration’s fitful campaign to address US voters’ affordability concerns ahead of the midterm elections is faltering, with some key efforts stalled, cast aside or limited in scope. 

The war in Iran has driven up gas prices and sent a chill through the spring housing market. It has also drowned out the administration’s set-piece events meant to highlight larger tax refunds and measures to lower drug prices.

Liz Pancotti, Managing Director of Policy and Advocacy at the Groundwork Collaborative, discusses how consumers are experiencing a spending slowdown. She speaks with Bloomberg's Kailey Leinz on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Warn Stalls Trump's Affordability Agenda

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Defense Department’s independent watchdog is declining to investigate a US Army helicopter flight near the home of musician Kid Rock and at a “No Kings” protest against President Donald Trump, according to a letter from the Pentagon’s new inspector general.
title: Pentagon Watchdog Declines to Probe Kid Rock Flights

author: Matthew Malinowski
description: Chilean President José Antonio Kast’s flagship economic bill cleared its first congressional hurdle on Thursday, but the vote gives the new administration little respite as it works to muster legislative support.
title: Chilean President Kast’s Mega Economic Bill Clears First Hurdle as Trouble Brews

author: Courtney McBride
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio approved the sale of hundreds of prized air-defense interceptors and other weapons to Middle East partners in deals worth $25.8 billion, three times the amount disclosed when the administration announced the agreements last week.
title: Rubio Approves $25.8 Billion in Weapons Push for Mideast Nations

author: Alberto Nardelli, Alex Wickham, Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump is forging ahead with plans to hold a summit with counterpart Xi Jinping next week in Beijing, despite unease among Chinese officials about holding the high-stakes meeting before the war in Iran is resolved.
title: Trump’s Summit With Xi Is On Despite China’s Iran Concerns

author: Augusta Saraiva, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: US President Donald Trump said he discussed trade and tariffs with Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva at the White House, and their two governments agreed to continue discussing the often-divisive issues.
title: Trump Praises Brazil’s Lula After Meeting on Tariffs, Trade

author: Rachel Schilke
description: Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) introduced a resolution Thursday that would amend the House rules to ban members and their staff from trading on prediction markets.
title: Prediction Market Ban for US House Members, Staff Gets GOP Push

author: Michael D McDonald, Erik Schatzker
description: Honduras’ new president is reviewing his predecessor’s agreements with China, a process that could help the US push to reduce the Asian nation’s influence in the region and lead to recognition of Taiwan.
title: Honduras Reviews China Ties Amid Push to Court US Investment

description: Newly inaugurated Honduran President Nasry Asfura is reviewing agreements made with China by his predecessor, Xiomara Castro, before deciding on restoring relations with Taiwan. Asfura spoke to Bloomberg's Erik Schatzker on May 6 on the sidelines of the Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Honduras’ New President Reviews China Ties

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The US sanctioned Iraq’s deputy oil minister and three militia leaders for exploiting the country’s oil sector and supporting Iranian-backed terrorist activity, ramping up pressure on Tehran and its regional proxies as the Trump administration seeks a deal to end a war in its 10th week.
title: US Sanctions Iraqi Oil Official, Militia Leaders Linked to Iran

author: James Regan
description: European Union prosecutors are investigating possible misappropriation of EU funds relating to media training for French far-right National Rally leader Jordan Bardella and other party members, Agence France-Presse reports, citing a person close to the case.
title: French Far-Right’s Bardella Linked to EU Funds Probe, Report Says

author: Scott Squires
description: Mexico is planning to invest 140 billion pesos ($8.1 billion) in new gas pipelines over the next four years, the latest step in President Claudia Sheinbaum’s plan to boost the country’s power generation.
title: Mexico Plans $8 Billion in Gas Pipelines to Boost Power Sector

author: Arvelisse Bonilla Ramos, Anthony Hughes
description: Hawkeye 360 Inc. soared 30% after the provider of satellite-based signals intelligence for US government agencies raised $416 million in a US initial public offering priced at the top of a marketed range.
title: Surveillance Firm Hawkeye 360 Jumps 30% After $416 Million IPO

author: Ewa Krukowska
description: Poland’s nationalist President Karol Nawrocki said he wanted to call a referendum on European Union climate policy in a move that’s bound to create fresh tensions with the pro-EU government and with Brussels.
title: Polish President Seeks Referendum on ‘Costly’ EU Climate Policy

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: Ukraine’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov arrived in the US for meetings with President Donald Trump’s envoys in a bid to reinvigorate stalled peace talks with Russia, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.
title: Zelenskiy’s Top Envoy Arrives in US to Renew Stalled Peace Talks

author: Dana Khraiche, Dan Williams
description: When the Lebanese militia Hezbollah entered the US-Israeli war against Iran by firing rockets and drones into Israel the day after the conflict began on Feb. 28, officials there saw in the crisis sweeping the region a chance to finally drive the militia, already weakened by a series of setbacks, away from Israel’s northern border. They’ve been loath to give it up.
title: How Israel’s Battle With Lebanon’s Hezbollah Fits Into the Iran War

author: Andrey Biryukov
description: Saudi Arabia brought forward some planned spending on infrastructure and food imports to soften the impact of the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a move that added to its budget deficit in the first quarter.
title: Saudi Arabia Boosted Logistics Spending to Blunt Impact of War

author: Slav Okov
description: Bulgaria’s incoming Prime Minister Rumen Radev proposed his cabinet lineup as he prepares to take office after a landslide election victory, breaking years of political deadlock.
title: Bulgaria’s Radev Picks Cabinet After Sweeping Victory

description: South Texas was the epicenter of Trump’s growing Latino support in 2024, but now those trends might be in reverse, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Ronald Brownstein says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Are Texas Latinos Turning on Trump?

author: Moses Mozart Dzawu
description: Ghana escalated a complaint over attacks on its citizens in South Africa, urging the African Union to weigh in after a spate of anti-foreigner protests fanned fears of xenophobic violence.
title: Ghana Petitions AU to Examine Xenophobic Attacks in South Africa

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazilian police are targeting Ciro Nogueira, a powerful senator and ally of former President Jair Bolsonaro, as part of their probe into Banco Master, expanding a sweeping investigation that has roiled the nation’s political system.
title: Brazil Police Target Ex-Bolsonaro Minister in Banco Master Probe

author: Raga Justin, Danielle Muoio Dunn
description: Hochul has resisted calls to raise income taxes on millionaires and large corporations ahead of competitive primary races.
title: NY Announces $268 Billion Budget Deal Including Second-Home Tax

author: Maciej Martewicz, Zosia Wanat
description: Poland will see nuclear power entering its energy mix in less than five years as small reactors gain traction in the European country, predicted billionaire Michal Solowow.
title: Billionaire Sees Poland’s Small Nuclear Reactors Online in 2030

author: Simon Marks, Mohammed Alamin
description: Sudan’s army is deploying more troops and anti-aircraft equipment near the Ethiopian border as it accuses Addis Ababa of backing its rebel opponents in a three-year civil war.
title: Horn of Africa Tensions Flare as Sudan Adds Forces Near Ethiopia

author: Michael Nienaber
description: The head of Germany’s Chambers of Commerce and Industry sharply criticized Chancellor Friedrich Merz for his poor reform record, calling the conservative leader’s ruling coalition dysfunctional and unreliable.
title: German Business Leader Criticizes Merz for Poor Reform Record

author: Flavia Rotondi, Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pope Leo XIV in the Vatican to discuss the conflict in the Middle East, following a public clash between the pontiff and President Donald Trump in recent weeks.
title: Rubio Discusses the Middle East With Pope After Trump Dispute

author: Patrick Sykes
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he met with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei in a rare public account of interactions with the country’s head of state who’s been in hiding since the start of the war with the US and Israel.
title: Iran’s President Says He Had Meeting With Injured Supreme Leader

author: Claire Jiao
description: Thailand and Cambodia pledged to rebuild bilateral relations, after long-simmering tensions erupted into deadly clashes last year, causing diplomatic ties between the Southeast Asian neighbors to be downgraded.
title: Thailand, Cambodia Pledge to Rebuild Ties After Deadly Clashes

author: Konrad Krasuski
description: The downfall of Poland’s biggest digital asset trading platform is causing trouble for Donald Trump’s ally in the presidential palace.
title: Demise of Crypto MAGA Sponsor in Poland Sparks Political Furor

author: Barbara Nascimento, Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil’s lower house approved a bill to regulate the exploration of critical and strategic minerals, a step toward realizing the potential of the nation’s vast reserves as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva prepares to meet Donald Trump.
title: Brazil House Backs Critical Minerals Bill as Lula Meets Trump

description: South Africa's government is turning up the pressure on Johannesburg, warning it could cut funding unless the city scraps a controversial wage deal. Bloomberg's Antony Sguazzin explains on Horizons Middle East & Africa. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Funding Cut Threat Looms Over Johannesburg

author: Alberto Brambilla
description: Leonardo SpA shareholders narrowly approved the Italian government’s board nominees, who overcame an unusually high level of opposition triggered by Rome’s decision to oust the chief executive officer.
title: Leonardo Investors Narrowly Back Meloni Board List After CEO Row

author: Ott Tammik
description: Officials on Europe’s eastern flank urged lawmakers to find sustainable sources of revenue to finance a massive surge in defense spending and avoid growing government borrowing across the continent.
title: Baltic States Warn of Unfunded Debt for Europe’s Defense Splurge

description: China on Thursday announced suspended death sentences for two former defense ministers convicted of graft, the first rulings since Chinese leader Xi Jinping started a sweeping military purge in 2023.

description: The issue that plagued Biden is now threatening to drag down Trump and the GOP
title: Affordability Concerns Rise as Trump, GOP’s Biggest Headache Grows

description: The Trump administration’s fitful campaign to address US voters’ affordability concerns ahead of the midterm elections is faltering, with some key efforts stalled, cast aside or limited in scope.

description: An oil-pumping station deep inside Russia could be on fire again just days after being hit by Ukrainian drones.

description: Political committees have already raised $4.7 billion for the November contests as ultra-wealthy donors look to shape the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency.
title: The Billionaires Behind the Most Expensive Midterm Elections in History

description: The Pentagon’s top acquisition official has assumed oversight of the Navy’s next-generation stealth fighter, people familiar with the matter said, indicating that Defense Department leaders have set aside earlier skepticism of the program.

description: The capture of a key Malian town by rebel forces last month poses a regional threat that requires foreign intervention to prevent the insurgency from spreading, Nigeria’s defense minister said.

author: Paul Wallace
description: The surge in energy costs is a major headache for Trump and American voters are increasingly against the war.

description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul discusses the US-Iran conflict, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's rift with President Donald Trump, the outlook for Germany's ruling coalition and the prospects for ending Russia's war with Ukraine. Wadephul talks with Bloomberg Editor-in-Chief John Micklethwait in Berlin. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Cambodia signaled a possible opening to ease Myanmar’s isolation within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, as sentiment by some members is warming toward bringing the crisis-worn nation’s leadership back into the fold.
title: Cambodia Signals Possible Asean Reopening for Myanmar Leaders
Merz-Trump Rift Was a 'Misunderstanding,' Wadephul Says (Video)

author: Arne Delfs
description: Germany’s top diplomat said the tension between President Donald Trump and Chancellor Friedrich Merz was a misunderstanding — and that the government in Berlin supports the US aim to ensure Iran can’t obtain a nuclear weapon.
title: German Top Diplomat Says Merz, Trump Have ‘Solid’ Relations

author: Godfrey Marawanyika
description: Zimbabwe said it was returning a number of foreign-owned farms that were seized during a violent land grab more than 25 years ago and pay compensation of $146 million.
title: Zimbabwe to Return 67 Foreign-Owned Farms Seized in Land Grab

description: The US is waiting on Iran to respond to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end a war that’s killed thousands of people, with tensions still high and Israel striking Lebanon’s capital on Wednesday.

author: Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal
description: The residents of Allentown are still sore about that Billy Joel song. While it’s true the Pennsylvania city became synonymous with deindustrialization after the US steel industry began its decline in the 1970s, Allentown should be known for more: In the 1950s, for instance, some of the first mass-produced transistors were made in the city, which were the precursor of today’s semiconductors. The city is also a unique logistics and e-commerce hub — it’s a day’s drive from nearly 40 percent of the
title: Odd Lots: How a US City Can Become a Manufacturing Hub (Podcast)

author: Shinhye Kang
description: North Korea has amended its constitution to formally give leader Kim Jong Un sole authority over the country’s nuclear arsenal, according to South Korean lawmakers briefed by Seoul’s spy agency.
title: North Korea’s New Constitution Gives Kim Formal Power Over Nukes

description: The US presented a one-page memorandum of understanding to Iran that would gradually reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the American blockade on Iranian ports, according to a person familiar with the measure. The move came after US President Donald Trump suspended a short-lived mission to offer safe passage for commercial ships through the waterway. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Weighs One-Page US Memorandum to End War

description: An intercontinental ballistic missile showcased by Turkey at an expo this week has a range of 6,000 kilometers (3,750 miles), putting much of Europe and the Middle East within reach. The Yildirimhan missile, named after an Ottoman sultan, marks progress toward joining the global military elite. Bloomberg's Onur Ant reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Missile Unveiled by Turkey Has a Range of 6,000 Kilometers

author: Deana Kjuka
description: Russia told foreign governments and organisations to evacuate diplomatic staff and citizens from Kyiv, saying a retaliatory strike would be inevitable if Ukraine tried to attack Moscow during May 9 World War II Victory Day celebrations.
title: Russia Urges Foreigners to Leave Kyiv Over Victory Day Threat

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union failed to finalize a long-delayed US trade deal during overnight talks, despite warnings from President Donald Trump that he would soon impose fresh tariffs.
title: EU Fails to Finalize US Trade Deal Despite Trump’s Demands

author: Lucille Liu
description: Senator Steve Daines expressed his appreciation toward Beijing for encouraging Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as the US searches for an off-ramp to a nine-week war that’s roiled global energy markets.

author: Alexander Weber
description: For Europe, a new cycle of Chinese rivalry heralded by its latest roadmap for advancement is forcing soul searching on how to respond.
title: European Industry Is in Crosshairs of China’s New Five-Year Plan

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon, Claire Jiao, Andreo Calonzo
description: Southeast Asian leaders are gathering in the Philippines for an annual summit, seeking to bolster economic cooperation and shore up regional resilience as countries grapple with an energy shock tied to the US-led war in Iran.
title: Crisis-Weary Southeast Asia Gathers Amid Iran War Energy Shock

description: The US and Iran are circling around a fresh proposal to end the war, as President Donald Trump searches for an exit from the Middle East conflict. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US and Iran Weigh Potential Deal to End the War

author: Miaojung Lin, Yian Lee
description: A company operating in China apparently fired the relative of a Taiwanese minister over backing for the island’s independence, according to Chinese state media — a move officials in Taipei condemned.
title: Taiwan Rebukes China After Report Firm Fired Minister’s Relative

author: Josh Wingrove
description: White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles said the US government would refrain from choosing winners and losers in artificial intelligence, the latest signal from a top aide to President Donald Trump as his administration prepares new AI policy directives.
title: Top Trump Aide Says Administration Won’t Pick Winners in AI Race

author: Molly Smith, Yoshiaki Nohara
description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will spend three days in Japan starting Monday and is expected to meet senior officials including Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi before traveling to China, according to local media reports.
title: Bessent to Meet Takaichi, Katayama, Ueda in Japan Next Week

author: John Liu
description: China’s financial regulator advised the country’s largest banks to temporarily suspend new loans to five refiners recently sanctioned by the US over their ties to Iranian oil, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: China Asks Banks to Pause New Loans to US-Sanctioned Refiners

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Jack Lew, former US Ambassador to Israel under President Joe Biden, says pushing Iran to "zero enrichment" would be a step beyond the 2015 nuclear deal, while emphasizing the need for strict monitoring and removal of enriched uranium. Marc Short, former Chief of Staff to Vice President Mike Pence and now Chairman of Advancing American Freedom, says heavy Republican spending against fellow GOP candidates could "demoralize" voters and backfire in November, as members grow increasingly fearful of crossing President Trump.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil, Gas Plunge As Iran Weighs US Proposal to End War | Balance of Power: Late Edition 05/06/2026
